:::{#exm-nb-mixture-moments}
#### Simulating a Poisson mixture

In @exm-nb-reg, $\mu = 4$ and $\rho = 2$.
By @thm-nb-mixture-moments,
any positive $\Lambda$ with mean $4$ and variance $4^2 / 2 = 8$
mixes Poisson counts into counts with mean $4$ and variance $4 + 8 = 12$,
matching @exm-nb-reg.
The first term, $4$, is the Poisson variation around each $\Lambda$;
the second term, $8$, is the variation of $\Lambda$ itself.

We can check this result by simulation,
drawing $\Lambda$ from a distribution with mean $4$ and variance $8$
and then drawing $Y$ given $\Lambda$:

```{r}
#| label: nb-mixture-sim
#| code-fold: show
set.seed(1)
nb_lambda <- rgamma(1e6, shape = 2, rate = 0.5)
c(mean = mean(nb_lambda), var = var(nb_lambda))
nb_y <- rpois(1e6, nb_lambda)
c(mean = mean(nb_y), var = var(nb_y))
```

The simulated $\Lambda$ values have sample mean about $4$ and variance about $8$,
and the simulated counts have sample mean about $4$ and variance about $12$,
three times the variance of Poisson counts with the same mean.
:::
